items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Terminology 67:1
items.html: (To the question) What are the twelve constellations? The Yesod of ZA is called the firmament, and every firmament means that it separates and joins; and since the Yesod of ZA is its end, it is found separating between the world of the male and the world of the female, and therefore it is called the firmament. However, their joining also depends on it, in the secret of the Life of the worlds, which is alive in the two worlds, in the secret of the nine of the direct light from above downward, clothed in the nine of the returning light from below upward, as above in Answer 51, see there. And it is known that there is no absence in the spiritual, and no transfer from place to place applies to it, and it is found that that same stature of the nine Sefirot that it bestows to the Nukva remains fixed in the Yesod of ZA, since it passed through there. And on this the Zohar hinted, that in this firmament are fixed the stars and the constellations, the sun and the moon, which are aspects branching out in his stature of nine Sefirot that are bestowed to the Nukva. Stars means: the GAR of the stature, drawn from the aspect of the inheritance of Aba and Ima, from the aspect of the MEM of the Tzelem, which are the upper KHB of the Mochin, and since from these KHB ZA receives only drop by drop, as above in Answer 62, therefore they are discerned in the aspect of stars, which appear like a likeness of sparks of lights. And the twelve constellations means: the aspect of the coupling of the two crowns of the Mochin, called Daat, which are the aspect of their VAK: the crown of Hesed, the Tifferet, and the crown of Gevura is the Yesod, as above in Answer 14, see there. And they are called constellations, after the crown of Gevura, which is the Yesod called Mazal, and it is because the crown of Hesed, which is the Tifferet, is not revealed from its own aspect as it shines in the Mochin in the place of their coming out in the upper Aba and Ima, where the Tifferet bears the illumination of Hochma without any sheath, but it shines to the measure of the Mazal, which is the Yesod that bears the screens of narrow and short, and therefore the Tifferet too is called by the name Mazal. And their being twelve in number is to hint that there are only six of them from above downward and six from below upward, which are twelve. And this does not mean that they lack the GAR, for all that is discussed here is in the stature of the AB of ZA, namely in the Mochin of birth. Rather, the intention is to distinguish between the KHB and the two crowns, of which from the two crowns, which are VAK, he takes the aspect of their actual essence, for they are the main roots of ZA, and Aba and Ima have no share in them except only from the aspect of the ascent of the MAN. And from this aspect they are the twelve constellations. But the stars, which are the drops drawn from the KHB, are entirely the share and essence of Aba and Ima, and ZA has no share in them except what his MAN causes them to have the stature of Hochma, for Bina does not receive Hochma except through the Tifferet that joins to her, as in the ten Sefirot of the direct light; therefore ZA takes a share in their KHB, and from this aspect they are the stars. Therefore in the aspect of the stars there is a complete stature of nine Sefirot, since they are the aspects of KHB; but in the constellations, whose root begins from the Tifferet, which is ZA, the GAR are not considered essential in them. However, surely in the constellations too there is the illumination of the GAR. And the aspect of the sun and the moon, they are the aspect of the two crowns above, in their root, in the place of the coming out of the Mochin in AA, where the Tifferet, called the sun, shines in all the complete perfection, without any sheath, and therefore it is not discerned there by the name crown of Hesed, which hints at its restriction to the measure of the screens in the Yesod, as above, but it is called sun, to indicate that it is the only root from which all the lights in the worlds are drawn. And the aspect of the crown of Gevura stands there below it and does not cover it, and therefore it is called there by the name moon. However, these sun and moon do not illuminate in this firmament in revelation, but in the aspect of concealment, and therefore they are referred to in it by the name the hidden sun and moon. For the sun is not revealed without a sheath, except after the correction in the seventh millennium, as is known. (Item 79).
